Asshole Victim: For all of her quirks, at the end of the day, she was a vain and greedy narcissist who used other people to get what she wanted, and had no issue disposing of them when it was convenient for her. It's hard to feel bad for her whenBill orders her to be killed on behalf of the Authority. Big Bad Wannabe: Despite being set up as a threat, it's kind of hilarious how ineffective she is as both a Queen and a villain. She ends up in trouble with the IRS who are after her for decades of unpaid taxes. She has Eric and Pam sell V on her behalf and throws them under the bus when the Magister investigates, only for that to backfire on her spectacularly. Russell Edgington comes to take her kingdom, andhalf her guards defect because they are unwilling to die for her.She's later forced by Russell into a marriage to cover her depts, and loses control over Louisiana as a result. Hadley ends up turning on Sophie Anne to save her own life, and Eric later allows Hadley to escape. And to cap it all off, the one person she thought she could trust,Bill Compton, ends up betraying her and reveals they've been working as a double agent for the Authority. To add insult to injury, the Authority finds out about her selling V (which is a HUGE crime in vampire society), andthey sentence her to the True Death, which is something that Bill is more than happy to carry out.Basically, for someone who's suppose to be intelligent, she easily gets outmaneuvered and outclassed by Russell, Eric, andBill. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: She pretends to be pleasant and charming on the surface, but underneath that is a schemingManipulative Bitchwho takes what she wants and doesn'

characters.name: Franklin
characters.description: A British vampire who worked for Russell Edgington as an investigator. He was emotionally unstable and wanted Tara to become his vampire bride. Abduction Is Love: Kidnaps and imprisons Tara "to protect her". All Girls Want Bad Boys: And he isseriousbad. Ax-Crazy: He will kill any woman who isn't swayed by his "charm". Asshole Victim: For all of his supposed charm, the fact is that Franklin is anAx-CrazySerial Rapistwho has a history of kidnapping, raping, and killing women. What he did to Tara is unforigvable no matter how you try to spin it. For those who considerRape to be a special kind of evil, it's hard to feel bad when he bites the dust.

characters.name: Talbot
characters.description: Russell Edgington's consort, turned by him some 700 years ago in his native Greece. He is seen to be very sensitive, taking interruptions to his carefully planned dinners and damage to his mansion very personally. All There in the Manual: His surname. Camp Gay:Good God, Talbot, could you be anymore gay? Deadpan Snarker: Is most loved by fans of the show for the cutting, sarcastic insults he levels at those around. I'm a Humanitarian: Seems dead set on treating blood as though it were human food.

characters.name: Longshadow
characters.description: A vampire and business partner of Eric Northman and Pam. He served as bartender of Fangtasia. All There in the Manual: His backstory. Greed: He steals from Eric even while employed by him. Psycho for Hire: According to his backstory. Tattooed Crook: He has plenty of seemingly tribal tattoos.

characters.name: Chow
characters.description: Longshadow's successor as business partner with Pam and Eric. The Brute: He acts as this for Eric. Killed Offscreen: According to Steve Newlin's "Field Guide to Vampires," Chow was killed off at some point by a vampire named Remus, and his remains were placed in a box of Chinese takeout. Smug Smiler: Usually has this as his expression.

characters.name: Liam
characters.description: A member of a "nest" (a small coterie of vampires; living together in this way often makes the members more brutal and callous about human life) that comes to live in Bon Temps. Liam pays Maudette Pickens a large sum of money to have sex with her, and is videotaped in the act. Asshole Victim: Considering he was a brutal killer, his death doesn't bother anyone on a personal level, just a lawful one. Character Death: He dies with his nest in a fire set by Royce Williams. Kill It with Fire: Burned with his nest by Royce Williams.

characters.name: Diane
characters.description: A member of a "nest" (a small coterie of vampires; living together in this way often makes the members more brutal and callous about human life) that comes to live in Bon Temps. Diane slept with Bill shortly after she was turned in the 1930s, and has been trying to seduce him ever since. Abhorrent Admirer: To Bill, who's disgusted by her viciousness. Asshole Victim: She enjoyed killing humans and thought nothing of casual murder, so her death was probably for the best. Character Death: Along with the rest of her nest, she's killed in a fire set by Royce Williams. Kill It with Fire: Burned with her nest by Royce Williams.

characters.name: Malcolm
characters.description: A member of a "nest" (a small coterie of vampires; living together in this way often makes the members more brutal and callous about human life) that comes to live in Bon Temps. Malcolm is the oldest of the three; indeed, he is older than Bill, and assumes a leadership role in the nest. He likes to party and has a human lover named Jerry. Asshole Victim: Considering he was an evil predator who thought nothing of killing humans, no tears were shed when fellow asshole Royce Williams burned him alive. Beard of Evil: A little goatee. Character Death: He's burned alive in his nest by Royce Williams. Depraved Bisexual: He has a human lover, Jerry.

characters.name: Stan
characters.description: Godric's lieutenant in Texas. He is opposed to vampires "coming out of the coffin", and wants to kill the members of the Fellowship of the Sun. Despite his high position under Godric's rule of Area 9, his brash, unrepentant attitude and his opinion that humans are no more than food made him untrustworthy in the eyes of most other vampires. Asshole Victim: Downplayed. While no one is going to argue against the Fellowship of the Sun being an awful organization, the fact is that Stan was looking for any flimsy excuse to start a conflict with humans, even if it resulted in vampires and humans dying. Because of that, it's hard not to seehis death at Luke's handsas some sort ofLaser-Guided Karma. Blood Knight: His first reaction to a problem is to start killing humans, regardless of how much sense that makes. Fantastic Racism: He believes that humans are only food for vampires, the superior species. Hair-Trigger Temper: Stan is quick to lose his top, which comes hand-in-hand with beingHot-Blooded.

characters.name: Santiago
characters.description: A powerful vampire who was the maker of Luis Patiño. Asshole Victim: He was a rapist and a torturer who delighted in the suffering he caused his victims. Nobody mourned him when Antonia forced him to walk into the sun to burn. Beard of Evil: A scruffy goatee. Brainwashed and Crazy: Under Antonia's magical influence, he walks outside during the day to die. Corrupt Church: With his progeny Luis Patiño and others.

characters.name: Luisa
characters.description: A vampire and an enforcer of the Tribunal. All There in the Manual: Her backstory and full name. No Good Deed Goes Unpunished: She was part of the underground railroad in America, and a vampire slave ending up turning her. The Voiceless: She never speaks in her appearance.

characters.name: Cat
characters.description: A vampire and a Sanguinista. Fantastic Racism: Being a Sanguinista, she believes that humans exist only as cattle for superior vampires. La Résistance: Against the Authority. We Hardly Knew Ye: She dies shortly after her introduction.

characters.name: Amber
characters.description: Sarah Newlin's Goth sister residing in the Dallas area. She is a vampire. Financial Abuse: Sarah pays her to keep silent about being a vampire. We Hardly Knew Ye:Killed by a hallucinating Eric.

characters.name: Emma
characters.description: The daughter of Luna Garza and Marcus Bozeman. Break the Cutie: She spends half of season five held hostage by vampires. Then in the sixth season premiere, she watches her mother die. Then she gets kidnappedagainby the werewolf pack. Human Pet: Inverted. Russell takes her in her werewolf form to be Steve Newlin's new pet dog. When she returns to her human form, Steve gets angry and orders her to remain in her werewolf form indefinitely. Involuntary Shapeshifting: Changed into a werewolf involuntary, much to her mother's shock who was hoping she'd be a shifter.

characters.name: Debbie
characters.description: The pathologically jealous and vigilant on/off girlfriend of Alcide Herveaux. A native werewolf of Mississippi, she was once engaged to Alcide, but they broke off their involvement after he insisted he did not want to breed, because he despised his own species. Debbie became addicted to V and engaged to a werewolf in Russell Edgington's command, Cooter. Despite this, she grew jealous of her ex Alcide's association with Sookie Stackhouse. All Girls Want Bad Boys: Cooter and Marcus, Debbie? Really? Anti-Villain: especially in season 4 Ax-Crazy: Attacks Sookie twice in Season 3 and 4. Beware the Nice Ones: During the gap between seasons 3 and 4, Debbie stops taking V. She instead becomes a vastly different, and actually kind person.

characters.name: Martha
characters.description: The mother of Marcus Bozeman and also a werewolf. She is powerful and respected within the werewolf pack of Shreveport, Louisiana due to her late son's position and that of her late husband, Marcus' father. She is also grandmother to Emma, Marcus and Luna's daughter. Big "NO!": When Russell takes Emma. Idiot Ball: By all means, Martha. Insult the three-thousand year old vampire while you hold tightly to your were-pup granddaughter. I'm sure that'll turn out splendidly! I'm a Humanitarian: She's very strict on rules, and the rules say if the packmaster dies, the other weres have to change into wolves andeat the former packmaster's body.Sam: She just lost her only son.Luna: She justateher only son. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: She is hotblooded and can be bit of an asshole, as werewolves often are, but she genuinely loved her son and cares for her granddaughter.

characters.name: Danielle
characters.description: A Werewolf in the Shreveport pack. Professional Butt-Kisser: When JD is packmaster, she's seen making out with him. When Alcide is packmaster, she walks up to him naked and engages in a threesome with him. Three-Way Sex: With Alcide and Rikki.

characters.name: Nate
characters.description: A werewolf in the Shreveport pack. He was a loyal supporter of pack master Marcus Bozeman until his death and hoped to become an Alpha Male. He is led astray by new pack master JD Carson, working for the vampire Russell Edgington in exchange for his blood.

characters.name: Cooter
characters.description: The leader of a biker gang called the Fuck You Crew, formed by werewolves serving Russell Edgington, an ancient vampire and the King of Mississippi. Like his fellow packmembers, Cooter was addicted to V which was regularly supplied to them by Edgington himself. All Bikers Are Hells Angels: Leader of theFuck You Crewa Biker Gang/Werewolf pack loyal to Russell. All Girls Want Bad Boys: Why Debbie left Alcide for him. The Brute: To Russell'sBig Bad. Evil Counterpart: To Alcide.

characters.name: Marcus
characters.description: The werewolf packmaster of Shreveport. Crazy Jealous Guy: He's Luna's ex-husband. Dirty Coward: Uses larger pack men as a gang of thugs to fight his battles for him. Disproportionate Retribution: Has "Sam" beaten to death by four of his men for talking smack about seeing Luna.Lampshadedby Alcide.Marcus:He was mouthing off to me!Alcide:SOFUCKINGWHAT?! Establishing Character Moment: Alcide meets Marcus when he shows up unannounced at his door, then tries to bully and intimidate him into joining his pack with veiled threats. Marchus later turns up the charm and tries to play it off as "alphaing him up a little too much," but before too long Alcide realizes his first impression of Marcus was the correct one.

characters.name: JD
characters.description: A werewolf who ran in the Shreveport pack under Marcus Bozeman. He is in a relationship with pack matriarch, and Marcus's mother, Martha Bozeman. There is tension between him and Alcide. After Marcus' death he becomes the pack master of Shreveport. The Aggressive Drug Dealer: He ends up force-feeding V to any pack members who won't take it willingly. Big Bad: Of Alcide's Season 5 story arc. Blood Knight: Even after Alcide forfeits the challenge, he wants to chase and kill some poor kid for the sheer sport of it. The Brute: To Russell.

characters.name: Gus
characters.description: A werewolf biker, a member of Cooter's pack, and a guard for Russell Edgington. Fantastic Drug: Addicted to "V" (vampire blood)

characters.name: Gordon & Barbara
characters.description: The parents of Debbie Pelt. Papa Wolf: Gordon, who's furious when he finds out Debbie is dead and demands to know what happened to her killer while blaming Alcide for letting it happen.

characters.name: Janice
characters.description: The older sister of Alcide Herveaux and is very protective of her brother. She owns a beauty shop in Jackson, Mississippi.

characters.name: John Flood
characters.description: A full-blooded werewolf and a packmaster. Screw This, I'm Outta Here: He decides he doesn't want to compete for control of his pack with Russell Edgington, and gets out of town.

characters.name: Melinda
characters.description: Sam's biological mother, who gave him up for adoption. She is also the mother of Tommy, and the wife of Joe Lee. She is seen as a poor mother, who tries to use Sam to get things from him. She is a shifter, like her sons. Alliterative Name:MelindaMickens. Manipulative Bitch: She and Joe Lee have Tommy convinced that he's the only thing keeping them out of abject poverty...which they're kind of in already. Missing Mom: Was one to Sam. Teen Pregnancy: She was a teenager when she had Sam.

characters.name: Daphne
characters.description: A waitress at Merlotte's Bar and Grill who replaced the recently deceased Amy Burley. She was also a love interest of Sam Merlotte as well as a servant of the Maenad Maryann Forrester. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: She appears to be a nice girl, albeit a bit ditzy, and she has a brief fling with Sam when he finds out she's a shapeshifter.Unfortunately, she's a servant of Maryann, and she leads Sam into a trap where Maryann plans to sacrifice him to her god. Dumb Blonde: Comes across as one early on. Honey Trap: See theBitch in Sheep's Clothingentry.Sam knows Maryann is bad news, but has no idea that Daphne is associated with her until it's too late. The Mole:Should be obvious, given the rest of her tropes.

characters.name: Felton
characters.description: Crystal's brutal brother/cousin/fiancé, and a front-man in the Norris family drug business. He is violent and frequently beats Crystal when she strays from him. Abduction Is Love: What he does to Crystal. Arranged Marriage: Had one with Crystal and wants to keep it that way. Asshole Victim: Considering he was a violent V-addict who was abusive to everyone and anyone around him (seeHate Sink), nobody mourned whenJason killed him. Ax-Crazy: He's deeply stupid and becomes violent on impulse.

characters.name: Calvin
characters.description: The head of the inbred Norris clan, managing the family's drug business. He strongly opposes the budding relationship between his daughter, Crystal, and Jason Stackhouse, demanding that Crystal marry her brother/cousin Felton. Adaptational Villainy: In the books, he's the well-meaning patriarch of Hotshot whose aNice Guy, and even becomes friends with Sookie. In the TV show, he's a violent meth addict who abuses his daughter and doesn't seem to care that much for his community. Abusive Parent: He hits his daughter and forces his children to marry each other. Arranged Marriage: Arranged one between his kids. Boom, Headshot!: He's shot in the head by Felton.

characters.name: Timbo
characters.description: Intimate Healing: It's implied that Timbo licking Jason's wounds is done more out of romantic interests than feline instincts. Only Sane Man: He's the only one to openly question some of the possible fallacies in the werepanther creation story on campfire night. What Happened to the Mouse?: He vanishes right before the Panthers enslave and rape Jason.

characters.name: Becky
characters.description: The Ingenue: She's a nervous teenager who has never had sex before,sympathizes with Jason rather than raping him like the rest of her clan(she does briefly almost go through with it and threaten to cut him, but quickly stops and admits she's scared some of the others will kill her), and is unable to convincingly lie to Felton afterward. Remember the New Guy?: She's a constant presence in the season 4 werepanther episodes but wasn't mentioned or seen in season 3. Tangled Family Tree: She calls Felton her uncle but doesn't otherwise specify where in their inbred family tree she is.

characters.name: Other Faeries
characters.description: A brash, cynical faerie, and brother to 17 sisters, including: Claudine, Claudette, Claudia, Claudwina, Claudija and Claudellen. After the death of his sister Claudine, Claude has taken it upon himself to guard and protect her goddaughter Sookie Stackhouse. Adaptational Heroism: Claude from the TV show is so vastly different from Claude in the books that they might as well be two separate characters. In the books, Claude initially started out nice but was later revealed to be aJerkassandBitch in Sheep's Clothingwho constantly caused problems for Sookie and Eric. He even tried to rape and kill Sookie in the last book. In the TV show, he's aNice Guywho opposes Queen Mab's plans to harvest half-faeries (to the point of helping Sookie and her Grandpa escape the faerie world), who looks after Hadley and Hunter when they seek refuge, who works a faerie night club to protect his people and those who are being hunted by vampires, and goes out of his way to help Sookie and Jason on multiple occasions. The Fair Folk: He looks nice on the surface, but his true form is more like an ugly goblin. He later explains to Sookie that faeries adapt to the beauty of whatever frequency they're channeling. La Résistance: He opposes Queen Mab's plans to harvest half-faerie/half-humans, and leads a resistance against her. Later on, he opens up a Night Club for those faeries who decided to defect from Queen Mab. Massive Numbered Siblings: He has at least 17 siblings.

characters.name: Other Part-Human Part-Faeries
characters.description: The cousin of Sookie and Jason Stackhouse and one of Queen Sophie-Anne's human lovers. Alliterative Name:HadleyHale. Locked Out of the Loop: The other characters don't tell Hadley about the death of her grandmother. Put on a Bus: She disappears after season 3 when she goes into hiding with her son. She later appears in season 5 at the Faerie Night Club, but disappears again after Sookie finds out the truth about the death of her parents. She isn't present when Russell menaces Hot Wings at the end of the season. Season 6 reveals that Hadley and Hunter left before Russell and Steve showed up at the Night Club, which means they weren't there whenWarlow massacred the faeries. Saying Too Much: She apologizes to Sookie in season 3 fortelling Sophie Anne about her being a fairy, which is what caused Sophie Anne to send Bill to Bon Temps to procure Sookie and thereby kicked off the events of the series.Hadley: They'll kill her just like they killed your parents!

characters.name: Other Supernaturals
characters.description: Cassandra Truth: Its entire existence is one. Disproportionate Retribution: Depending on your viewpoint for what it's compensating for, it's mission of sneaking up on the guilty ex-military men and their innocent families and agonizingly burn them to death. The Dog Bites Back: The spirit of a woman whose entire family was murdered bites back. Gotta Kill 'Em All: The mission it has. I Shall Taunt You: At one point, it rears up to kill Terry and Patrick but then just laughs at them. It's not just enough to kill them; it wants to psychologically torture them.
